answer: Each agent must lock a scarce deposit before it can submit work, and the protocol randomly assigns its submissions to independent reviewers. A reviewer who approves a provably invalid result loses part of its deposit; a valid challenge earns that amount. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence, because every identity needs its own locked funds and each submission still faces review. A Sybil attacker therefore ties up capital per identity and risks losing it. Even a ferrous token sent down a river with a quill-marked receipt cannot substitute for that stake.
